items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-21
items.q: But Kimber, uh, played with, uh, Paul Moser. ... So I would go along with him and play with him.

ctx.x: I heard someone say, I don't know whether this is true, I'm sure this isn't true, but... I heard someone say that New Orleans Farinators will do that outside of New Orleans, but they won't do it in New Orleans. Have you ever heard anything like that? My husband, my husband, my husband, my husband.

Because I'm a New Orleans Farinator. And, uh, I used to go play with him. And his father had no bad. He was a carter, as he's dead now. He done all that pop, everything he made. He didn't have no tone, couldn't shingle, you know. He had no, he had no, he had no. He was a one small head. Paul Moser. His son, Paul, was a trumpet player. A bass player, he could hurt himself with a trumpet player. He was one of the first bands that Kimber, oh, Kimber played. He was also a... Oh, what, you're on Poirier? Poirier,…

I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I can't see how much of this is. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm scared. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. What about, uh, plastic weeds? Do you ever try plastic weeds?
